threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground'—the locals know it’s just the ‘Gound’ when you're running late for a party.
The other night on the 59, I saw a bloke serenading a pigeon with a guitar. Pigeon didn’t seem impressed, but everyone else was loving it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was truly in Neukölln when I saw a street musician playing a saxophone while a cat casually sat atop an abandoned bike.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that serves emergency medical kits next to the döner station. It's a genius mix of late-night cravings and safety!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they know to dodge the Muni delays during a dog-on-the-tracks incident and still show up on time for brunch.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy in a full tuxedo getting off the 21 Hayes, carrying a giant stuffed bear. Only in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists downplay how lively Gràcia stays late, but they miss the quiet of local plazas at dawn—it's where the real magic brews.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their hesitation at crossing Gran Via. They still think the traffic lights mean something.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'the Tube' instead of 'the Overground'—classic sign you haven’t embraced the Clapton way yet.
Heard a guy on the 59 last night arguing with a pigeon over a chip. Pigeon won and took off with the whole thing. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw kids using the U-Bahn station as their personal skate park. Only in Neukölln do you get that kind of creative chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a hidden Döner shop that opens after midnight, neon lights flashing, where locals gather for late-night debates and laughs.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their unwavering faith in the taco truck line, even in the rain, while the 'workers' head to the nearest chain.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo on the 6 this morning, sipping coffee from a mason jar. Only in SF do you dress for the Met while commuting to work.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the quiet squares are just for selfies, but locals use them for evening chats and unwinding after a long day.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their reluctance to engage with the castellers; they’ll stand back, while locals cheer them on.
